name: Black-shouldered Nightjar
reason: The 2009 Fiery-necked Nightjar note explicitly includes nigriscapularis. Its assigned Avibase ID has a narrower scope.

name: White-eyed Gull
reason: The 2009 edition explicitly excludes the unsubstantiated White-eyed Gull record in its omitted-species section.

name: Arctic Tern
reason: The 2009 edition discusses Arctic Tern in its omitted-species section and excludes it from checklist membership.

name: Eurasian (Great) Bittern
reason: No Eurasian Great Bittern account in the 2009 checklist. Little Bittern is a different species.

name: Christmas Island Frigatebird
reason: EARC accepted the historical record in its 2016 report. Reviewers later recommended rechecking the original images.

name: Crested (Oriental) Honey Buzzard
reason: No Crested Honey Buzzard account in the 2009 checklist. Its European Honey Buzzard is a different species.

name: Thick-billed Honeyguide
reason: The 2009 Lesser Honeyguide note explicitly includes conirostris. The 2019 Avibase group has a wider stated scope.

name: Racquet-tailed Roller
reason: No Racquet-tailed Roller or Coracias spatulatus account in the 2009 checklist.

name: Rock Kestrel
reason: The 2009 Common Kestrel account names the resident race rufescens and its Rock Kestrel name.

name: Tropical Boubou
reason: The 2009 omitted-species discussion explicitly retains major under Tropical Boubou.

name: Weyn’s Weaver
reason: No Weyn’s Weaver or Ploceus weynsi account in the 2009 checklist.

name: Shelley’s Sparrow
reason: The 2009 Kenya Rufous Sparrow note includes race shelleyi.

name: Western Citril
reason: The 2019 Western Citril was historically treated under citrinelloides. The 2009 African Citril account only names kikuyuensis, so inclusion of frontalis is uncertain.

name: Lesser Whitethroat
reason: No Lesser Whitethroat account in the 2009 checklist. Common Whitethroat is a different species.

name: Mbulu White-eye
reason: The Mbulu White-eye may have been included in the old Montane White-eye complex. Its 2009 coverage is uncertain.

name: Matsudaira’s Storm-petrel
reason: The 2009 list cites two 1981 sightings off Mombasa. The atlas digitization treats the records as uncertain (Taylor, 1982; Hunter, 2019).

name: Brown-headed Apalis
reason: Listed in 2009 and absent from the 2019 checklist. The reason for omission is unconfirmed.

name: Cotton Pygmy Goose
reason: Reported at Lake Baringo in 2026, apparently involving one bird.

name: Ruddy Shelduck
reason: Historical report from Laikipia in 1986.

name: Vinaceous Dove
reason: Kenyan record from May 2022.

name: Brown Skua
reason: Historical report from August 1961.

name: Little Gull
reason: Kenyan sighting documented in eBird.

name: Sabine's Gull
reason: Kenyan record from January 2024.

name: Caspian Gull
reason: Multiple Kenyan sightings documented in eBird.

name: Red-billed Tropicbird
reason: Kenyan record from March 2022.

name: Red-tailed Tropicbird
reason: An October 1982 report describes a conspicuous red tail.

name: Persian Shearwater
reason: Reviewers consider Persian Shearwater the likely Kenyan form. The 2019 account gives no diagnostic details.

name: Böhm's Bee-eater
reason: Kenyan sighting documented in eBird.

name: Ethiopian Bee-eater
reason: The 2019 row prints Merops lafresnayii under a different Avibase ID.

name: Melodious Lark
reason: Melodious Lark Mirafra cheniana is absent from the 2019 checklist. Rattling Cisticola Cisticola chiniana is unrelated.

name: Ethiopian Cisticola
reason: The 2019 Winding Cisticola account gives no subspecies. eBird reports include multiple birds.

name: Bamboo Warbler
reason: The 2019 account leaves coverage uncertain. eBird reports include several birds.

name: Yellow-eyed Bristlebill
reason: The 2019 Red-tailed Bristlebill account does not name ugandae.

name: Green White-eye
reason: The 2019 account refers to the broader African Yellow White-eye.

name: Broad-ringed White-eye
reason: Kenyan record from May 2021. The 2019 Montane White-eye account names the Kulal form.

name: Yellow-breasted Forest Robin
reason: A historical specimen is documented. Its significance for the Kenyan checklist remains uncertain.

name: Siberian Stonechat
reason: The 2019 stonechat account covers the African concept. Later Siberian Stonechat sightings are documented in eBird.

name: Arnot's Chat
reason: Kenyan record from December 2022.

name: Gosling's Bunting
reason: Kenyan record from May 2022.

name: Speckled Tinkerbird
reason: The Kakamega sighting is unsubstantiated and the reported Kitale specimen is untraced (Zimmerman et al., 1996).

name: Hybrid Lovebird
reason: AviList does not list the Fischer’s × Yellow-collared Lovebird swarm as a species.

name: Great Grey Shrike
reason: Reviewers traced the historical locality to what appears to be South Sudan.
